title: Reasonableness from the smallest positive atom
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. If $m$ is the smallest probability of any point of positive probability under $p$, then $X$ is reasonable with constant $1/m$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
